Statement 2: Unlike the Presidential election, the electoral college for the Vice President includes nominated members of both Houses of Parliament. Which of the statements above is/are correct ?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements regarding the current Vice President of India:
Statement 1: Chandrapuram Ponnusami (C.P.) Radhakrishnan is the Vice President of India, took charge on 12th September 2025.
Statement 2: Unlike the Presidential election, the electoral college for the Vice President includes nominated members of both Houses of Parliament.
Which of the statements above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both Statements 1 and 2 are correct

Key Points

  • Statement 1: Chandrapuram Ponnusami (C.P.) Radhakrishnan is the Vice President of India, took charge on 12th September 2025. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • Statement 2: The electoral college for the Vice President of India includes members (both elected and nominated) of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, unlike the Presidential election, where nominated members are excluded. This is correct as per Article 66 of the Indian Constitution. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
  • The Vice Presidential election process is clearly defined in the Indian Constitution, ensuring representation from both Houses of Parliament.
  • The Vice President serves as the Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha and is elected for a term of 5 years.
  • The election is conducted using a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote, ensuring fairness in the voting process.

Additional Information

  • Vice President of India:
    • The Vice President is the second-highest constitutional office in India.
    • The office was established under Article 63 of the Indian Constitution.
    • The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
    • In the event of a vacancy in the office of the President, the Vice President acts as the President until a new President is elected.
  • Electoral College for Vice Presidential Election:
    • As per Article 66(1) of the Constitution, the Vice President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament.
    • Unlike the Presidential election, the electoral college for the Vice President includes nominated members of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
  • Eligibility Criteria:
    • A candidate for the Vice President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be elected as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
    • The candidate must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or any state government.
  • Tenure and Removal:
    • The Vice President is elected for a term of 5 years but can continue in office until a successor assumes charge.
    • The Vice President can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority in the Rajya Sabha and agreed upon by the Lok Sabha.
  • Important Articles Related to the Vice President:
    • Article 63: Provides for the office of the Vice President.
    • Article 64: States that the Vice President shall be the ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.
    • Article 66: Deals with the election of the Vice President.

Important Points

  • Comparison with Presidential Elections:
    • The President is elected by an electoral college comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of states and Union territories (with legislatures), excluding nominated members.
    • In contrast, the Vice President is elected solely by the members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members.
  • Historical Note:
    • Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was the first Vice President of India (1952–1962) and later became the President.
    • Many Vice Presidents have played crucial roles in Indian politics, often contributing significantly as Chairpersons of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Read the below statements: 1. NASA launched a space telescope, SPHEREx, to study the universe's "cosmic glow". 2. The Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) telescope was inaugurated at Hanle, Ladakh. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.questionHtml:
Read the below statements:
1. NASA launched a space telescope, SPHEREx, to study the universe's "cosmic glow".
2. The Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) telescope was inaugurated at Hanle, Ladakh.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 and Statement 2 both.

Key Points

  • NASA launched the SPHEREx space telescope:
    • SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer) is a space telescope developed by NASA.
    • Its primary goal is to study the universe’s "cosmic glow," also known as the background infrared radiation.
    • The mission will help scientists understand the formation and evolution of galaxies, the distribution of water and organic molecules in space, and the history of the universe.
    • SPHEREx will map the sky in 96 different color bands to capture a detailed view of the cosmos. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • MACE telescope inaugurated at Hanle, Ladakh:
    • The Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) telescope is one of the largest gamma-ray telescopes in the world.
    • It was installed at Hanle, Ladakh, which is home to India’s high-altitude astronomical observatory.
    • The telescope is designed to detect Cherenkov radiation, which occurs when high-energy gamma rays interact with the Earth’s atmosphere.
    • This facility strengthens India’s position in the field of gamma-ray astronomy and contributes to the study of cosmic phenomena such as pulsars, supernovae, and black holes. Hence, statement 2 is correct.

Additional Information

  • SPHEREx Mission:
    • Full Form: Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer.
    • Launch Year: Planned for 2025.
    • It will survey the entire sky four times, collecting data from over 300 million galaxies and 100 million stars in the Milky Way.
    • SPHEREx will help identify the building blocks of life by studying the distribution of water and organic molecules in the interstellar medium.
    • Cosmic Infrared Background: The mission aims to decode the history of star formation and galaxy evolution through infrared observations.
  • MACE Telescope:
    • Location: Hanle, Ladakh, India.
    • Primary Function: Detects Cherenkov radiation to study high-energy cosmic gamma rays.
    • Operational Altitude: Situated at an altitude of approximately 4,300 meters above sea level.
    • Significance: Supports research in astrophysics, including studies on gamma-ray bursts, supernova remnants, and active galactic nuclei.
    • Global Importance: It is one of the largest telescopes of its kind, enhancing international collaboration in gamma-ray astronomy.
  • Gamma-ray Astronomy:
    • Purpose: Focuses on studying celestial phenomena emitting gamma rays, the highest-energy form of electromagnetic radiation.
    • Applications: Helps explore black holes, neutron stars, and the origins of cosmic rays.
    • Detection Technique: Cherenkov telescopes detect gamma-ray interactions with the Earth’s atmosphere through light flashes called Cherenkov radiation.
    • Global Facilities: Other major gamma-ray observatories include the High Energy Stereoscopic System (HESS) in Namibia and the VERITAS observatory in the USA.

Important Points

  • Hanle Observatory:
    • Operated by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA).
    • Home to other key facilities like the Indian Astronomical Observatory and the Himalayan Chandra Telescope.
    • Known for its clear skies, making it an ideal location for high-altitude astronomy.
  • NASA Space Missions:
    • James Webb Space Telescope (JWST): Focuses on infrared astronomy and studying the formation of stars and galaxies.
    • Hubble Space Telescope: An iconic telescope known for its contributions to understanding the universe’s expansion and distant galaxies.
    • Chandra X-ray Observatory: Specializes in studying high-energy phenomena like black holes and supernovae.
    • SPHEREx continues NASA’s legacy of pioneering space observatories for understanding cosmic evolution.

questions.question: The 'Fortaleza Declaration' of 2014 is most famous in BRICS history for the creation of which of the following?

options.text: A permanent BRICS Secretariat in Brazil
options.html: A permanent BRICS Secretariat in Brazil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA).

Key Points

  • The Fortaleza Declaration of 2014 is a significant milestone in the history of the BRICS nations, as it led to the creation of the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA).
  • The CRA is a framework established to provide financial support to member countries during balance of payments crises or liquidity shortages.
  • It was officially launched during the 6th BRICS Summit held in Fortaleza, Brazil in July 2014.
  • The CRA has a total capital of USD 100 billion, with contributions as follows: China (USD 41 billion), Brazil, Russia, and India (USD 18 billion each), and South Africa (USD 5 billion).
  • This arrangement is designed to complement existing international financial safety nets, such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and strengthen the financial stability of BRICS nations.

Additional Information

  • What is BRICS?
    • BRICS is an acronym for Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, a group of emerging economies that collaborate on various political, economic, and social fronts.
    • Formed in 2009, South Africa joined the bloc in 2010.
    • The group focuses on economic cooperation, development, trade, and investment.
  • Significance of the CRA:
    • It helps BRICS nations manage short-term liquidity pressures and safeguard against potential financial crises.
    • It reduces dependency on Western-dominated financial institutions like the IMF or World Bank.
    • The CRA strengthens economic stability and fosters cooperation among BRICS countries.
  • Other Key Outcomes of the Fortaleza Declaration:
    • The establishment of the New Development Bank (NDB), headquartered in Shanghai, China, to fund infrastructure and sustainable development projects in BRICS and other emerging economies.
    • A focus on enhancing collaboration in areas such as healthcare, education, and science and technology.
    • Promotion of reforms in global financial institutions to ensure fair representation and decision-making power for emerging economies.
  • Comparison with Other Options:
    • A common BRICS currency called 'R5': No such currency was created during the Fortaleza Summit. However, discussions on enhancing trade in local currencies have occurred.
    • BRICS Space Agency: While the idea of collaboration in space technology exists, no dedicated space agency was formed under this declaration.
    • A permanent BRICS Secretariat in Brazil: No permanent secretariat was established in Brazil or any other member state as part of the Fortaleza Declaration.

Important Points

  • Fortaleza Summit: The 6th BRICS Summit, held in July 2014, emphasized economic cooperation and fostering a multipolar world order.
  • New Development Bank (NDB): The NDB is seen as an alternative to Western-dominated financial institutions, with an initial capital of USD 50 billion, expandable to USD 100 billion.
  • Global Financial Reforms: BRICS advocates for reforms in the governance structures of the IMF and World Bank to ensure fair representation for emerging economies.
  • Strengthening Cooperation: The Fortaleza Declaration highlighted the importance of cooperation in areas like energy, healthcare, education, and technology.

questions.question: Read the following statements regarding the 'Doctrine of Repugnancy' (Article 254): Statement I: If a ‘State law’ on a "Concurrent List" subject conflict with a ‘Union law’, then the Union law prevails, and the State law becomes 'void' to the extent of the repugnancy. Statement II: A State law on a Concurrent subject that conflicts with a Union law can still prevail within that State if it has been reserved for and received the assent of the President. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statements regarding the 'Doctrine of Repugnancy' (Article 254):
Statement I: If a ‘State law’ on a "Concurrent List" subject conflict with a ‘Union law’, then the Union law prevails, and the State law becomes 'void' to the extent of the repugnancy.
Statement II: A State law on a Concurrent subject that conflicts with a Union law can still prevail within that State if it has been reserved for and received the assent of the President.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.text: Both Statements I and II are correct
options.html: Both Statements I and II are correct

options.text: Neither Statement I nor II is correct
options.html: Neither Statement I nor II is correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both Statements I and II are correct.

Key Points

  • Statement I:
    Article 254 of the Indian Constitution deals with the 'Doctrine of Repugnancy'. It states that if there is a conflict between a State law and a Union law on a subject in the Concurrent List, the Union law will prevail, and the State law will be declared 'void' to the extent of the conflict.
    Hence, Statement I is correct.
  • Statement II:
    A State law on a subject in the Concurrent List that conflicts with a Union law can still prevail within the state if it is reserved for the President's assent and receives it. However, Parliament retains the power to override such a State law by enacting a subsequent Union law.
    Hence, Statement II is correct.
  • Concurrent List:
    The Concurrent List is one of the three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution. It contains subjects where both the Union and State Legislatures can legislate, such as education, marriage, divorce, and forests.
  • The Doctrine of Repugnancy ensures the supremacy of Union legislation in case of conflicts between Union and State laws on subjects in the Concurrent List.
  • Thus, both statements accurately describe provisions under Article 254 of the Indian Constitution.

Additional Information

  • Doctrine of Repugnancy:
    • It arises when laws enacted by the Union and a State on the same subject in the Concurrent List are inconsistent or in conflict.
    • The principle ensures that the law made by the Union Parliament prevails over the State law.
    • However, if the conflicting State law has received Presidential assent, it prevails in that State unless overridden by a subsequent Union law.
  • Article 254 of the Indian Constitution:
    • Sub-clause (1): States that if a State law is inconsistent with a Union law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law will prevail, and the State law will be void to the extent of the inconsistency.
    • Sub-clause (2): A State law that conflicts with a Union law can prevail in that State if it has been reserved for and received the President's assent.
    • However, Parliament can override such a State law by enacting a subsequent law on the same subject.
  • Seventh Schedule of the Constitution:
    • It divides legislative powers between the Union and State governments through three lists: the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
    • The Union List contains subjects like defense, foreign affairs, and atomic energy, where only the Union Government can legislate.
    • The State List includes subjects like police, public health, and agriculture, where only State Governments can legislate.
    • The Concurrent List includes subjects like criminal law, education, and marriage, where both Union and State Governments can legislate.
  • Examples of Presidential Assent:
    • The Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, which conflicted with Union laws, was reserved for and received the President's assent, allowing it to prevail in Bihar.
    • Similarly, State laws like the Maharashtra Rent Control Act have prevailed in Maharashtra after obtaining Presidential assent.

Important Points

  • Hierarchy of Laws: Union laws prevail over State laws in the Concurrent List, ensuring uniformity across the nation.
  • Presidential Assent: A State law conflicting with Union law can prevail only within the State if it has received the President's assent.
  • Parliament's Supremacy: Even after Presidential assent, Parliament can override the State law by enacting a subsequent law on the same subject.
  • Judicial Review: Courts have the power to examine the validity of conflicting laws and ensure compliance with Article 254.

questions.question: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961), often associated with the Mahalanobis Model, marked a significant shift in India's development strategy. What was the primary focus of this plan?
questions.questionHtml: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961), often associated with the Mahalanobis Model, marked a significant shift in India's development strategy. What was the primary focus of this plan?

options.text: Rapid industrialization with a particular emphasis on the development of basic and heavy industries.
options.html: Rapid industrialization with a particular emphasis on the development of basic and heavy industries.

options.text: Establishing an export-oriented economy to integrate rapidly with global trade markets.
options.html: Establishing an export-oriented economy to integrate rapidly with global trade markets.

options.text: Achieving immediate self-sufficiency in food grain production through the Green Revolution.
options.html: Achieving immediate self-sufficiency in food grain production through the Green Revolution.

options.text: Maximizing the role of the private sector in the 'commanding heights' of the economy.
options.html: Maximizing the role of the private sector in the 'commanding heights' of the economy.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rapid industrialization with a particular emphasis on the development of basic and heavy industries.

Key Points

  • The Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis Model, formulated by Indian statistician P.C. Mahalanobis. This model emphasized the need for rapid industrialization with a focus on heavy and basic industries.
  • The plan aimed to build a strong industrial base to drive long-term economic growth, reduce dependency on foreign imports, and generate employment opportunities.
  • Key sectors targeted included steel production, machine tools, heavy machinery, and infrastructure. Projects like the establishment of steel plants in Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur were initiated.

The correct answer is Both Statement 1 and Statement 2.

Key Points

  • Statement 1: The Dugong (Sea Cow) is protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which ensures the highest level of legal protection for species in India. Hence, Statement 1 is correct.
  • Statement 2: Being included under Schedule I means Dugong receives the same level of protection as the Tiger, as both are considered critically important for conservation. Hence, Statement 2 is correct.

  • Legal protection under Schedule I prohibits activities like hunting, capturing, or harming Dugongs, and violators face stringent penalties under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
  • The Dugong’s habitat, predominantly in shallow coastal waters like the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands, further necessitates robust legal protection.

Additional Information

    • Dugongs are primarily found in the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, which is a critical conservation site.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Joint ISRO–NASA mission using L and S-band radar.

Key Points

  • NISAR Mission is a collaborative project between NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) and ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation). It is designed to provide global, all-weather, high-resolution radar imaging of Earth.
  • The mission will use dual-frequency radar systems, specifically L-band and S-band radar, to generate accurate and detailed images of the Earth's surface.
  • The L-band radar is being developed by NASA, while the S-band radar is being developed by ISRO. Together, they will provide a unique capability to measure changes in Earth's land surface, ice sheets, and ecosystems.
  • The satellite is expected to monitor a wide range of phenomena, including land subsidence, deforestation, glacier movements, earthquakes, and agricultural patterns.
  • The launch of the NISAR satellite is planned to take place from India on an ISRO-built GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle).

Additional Information

  • Key Features of the NISAR Mission:
    • The NISAR satellite will have an advanced radar system capable of detecting changes as small as a centimeter in the Earth's surface.
    • Its primary objectives include studying climate change, natural disasters, and ecosystem dynamics.
    • The satellite will provide data that can help in disaster management, such as monitoring earthquakes and tsunamis.
    • The mission is expected to deliver data for a period of 3 years, with an anticipated launch date in the mid-2020s.
  • L-band vs. S-band Radar:
    • L-band radar operates at a frequency of 1–2 GHz and is suitable for penetration through vegetation, soil, and snow, making it ideal for studying land cover and deforestation.
    • S-band radar operates at a frequency of 2–4 GHz and provides higher resolution images, making it effective for monitoring soil moisture and agricultural patterns.
  • Applications of NISAR Data:
    • Monitoring glacier dynamics and ice sheet collapses to understand climate change impacts.
    • Studying land deformation caused by earthquakes, landslides, and volcanic activity.
    • Assessing agricultural yields and land use changes for better resource management.
    • Mapping coastal erosion and wetland ecosystems.
  • ISRO-NASA Collaboration:
    • This partnership leverages the technological expertise of both agencies. NASA contributes its experience with radar systems, while ISRO provides its expertise in low-cost satellite development and launches.
    • The collaboration strengthens international efforts in advancing Earth observation technologies.

Important Points

  • ISRO's Role:
    • ISRO is responsible for developing the S-band radar, the satellite bus, and the launch vehicle (GSLV).
    • ISRO's expertise in launching low-cost and reliable satellites makes it a key contributor to this joint mission.
  • NASA's Role:
    • NASA is developing the L-band radar and providing mission systems for data processing and management.
    • NASA's advanced radar technology enhances the satellite's ability to capture high-resolution images.
  • Significance of NISAR:
    • NISAR is the world’s most advanced radar imaging satellite for studying Earth's surface changes.
    • It represents a major step toward understanding global environmental challenges and developing sustainable solutions.

  • Break Intervals: There is a 2-minute break between the first and second quarters as well as the third and fourth quarters. A longer 15-minute halftime break is observed between the second and third quarters.
  • Overtime Rules: If the game ends in a tie after the fourth quarter, overtime periods of 5 minutes each are played until a winner is decided.
  • Comparison with Other Formats: FIBA’s format is different from the NBA, which uses four 12-minute quarters, and college basketball in the U.S., which typically has two 20-minute halves.

  • Shot Clock: FIBA uses a 24-second shot clock, which requires teams to attempt a shot within 24 seconds of gaining possession.
  • Global Popularity: FIBA’s rules are designed to maintain consistency in international competitions, ensuring fair play and standardization across countries.

The correct answer is Abolishing industrial licensing for most industries to encourage private entry.

Key Points

  • Liberalization, as introduced in the New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1991, aimed at reducing government restrictions and promoting private sector participation in the economy.
  • The abolition of industrial licensing was a core aspect of liberalization. It eliminated the need for government approval to establish or expand industries, except for a few sectors like defense and hazardous industries. This encouraged private entry and competition.
  • The focus of liberalization was on removing constraints like red tape and bureaucratic hurdles, which had previously slowed the growth of industries and discouraged entrepreneurship.
  • The policy also aimed at creating an environment conducive to foreign investment, technology transfer, and private sector-led growth by reducing government control.
  • Industrial licensing was retained only for strategic and sensitive sectors, marking a clear shift towards a market-driven economy. 
  • This measure significantly contributed to the expansion of private enterprises, improved efficiency, and fostered innovation in the Indian economy.

Additional Information

  • New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1991:
    • The NEP was introduced by the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao, with Dr. Manmohan Singh as the Finance Minister, to address India’s economic crisis in the early 1990s.
    • It focused on Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG) to revive the economy and make India globally competitive.
    • The policy encouraged foreign direct investment (FDI) and eased restrictions on imports and exports, aiming to integrate the Indian economy with the global market.
  • Industrial Licensing:
    • Prior to 1991, industrial licensing was mandatory under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, leading to excessive government control over business activities.
    • The abolition of licensing under liberalization removed barriers for entrepreneurs and allowed industries to operate with greater autonomy.
    • This change contributed to the rise of private sector enterprises and improved productivity across sectors.
  • Privatization:
    • Privatization was another major aspect of NEP 1991, involving the transfer of ownership of public sector enterprises to private entities.
    • The government reduced its stake in several Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and allowed private players to participate in areas previously reserved for the public sector.
  • Globalization:
    • Globalization aimed at integrating the Indian economy with the global market by reducing trade barriers, allowing foreign investment, and promoting exports.
    • The policy emphasized technology transfer, global partnerships, and market competition to improve efficiency and innovation.

Important Points

  • Key Objectives of Liberalization:
    • Reduce state intervention: Liberalization aimed at minimizing government interference in economic activities and providing greater autonomy to businesses.
    • Promote competition: By removing licensing restrictions, liberalization fostered healthy competition among industries, improving efficiency and innovation.
    • Encourage foreign investment: Liberalization created a favorable environment for FDI and foreign partnerships, leading to technology and capital inflow.
    • Boost private sector: The abolition of licensing allowed the private sector to expand and contribute significantly to India’s economic growth.
  • Impact of Liberalization:
    • India witnessed rapid industrial growth, especially in sectors like IT, telecommunications, manufacturing, and services.
    • It led to the emergence of globally competitive Indian companies and improved access to modern technologies.
    • Foreign companies established their presence in India, boosting employment and economic activity.

The correct answer is A - 2, B - 1, C - 3, D - 4.

Key Points

  • Second Schedule: It deals with the emoluments, allowances, and privileges of high-ranking officials such as the President, Governors, Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and others. Hence, A - 2 is correct.
  • Third Schedule: This schedule provides the forms of oaths and affirmations for various constitutional posts such as Union Ministers, Members of Parliament, Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts, etc. Hence, B - 1 is correct.
  • Fourth Schedule: It specifies the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) to different states and union territories. Hence, C - 3 is correct.
  • Seventh Schedule: It outlines the division of legislative powers between the Union and State governments under three lists – Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. Hence, D - 4 is correct.

Additional Information

  • Second Schedule:
    • It deals with the salaries, allowances, and privileges of officials such as the President, Vice President, Governors, Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts, Speaker of Lok Sabha, and others.
    • This schedule ensures uniformity and transparency in the remuneration of these officials.
    • It also defines the pension rights of some officials after retirement.
  • Third Schedule:
    • This schedule provides the format for oaths or affirmations to be taken by Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament, Judges, and others before assuming their respective offices.
    • The oaths emphasize loyalty to the Constitution of India and the commitment to discharge duties faithfully.
  • Fourth Schedule:
    • This schedule outlines the distribution of seats in the Rajya Sabha among states and union territories.
    • The allocation is based on the population of states and union territories as per the last census.
    • The Fourth Schedule ensures proportional representation in the Rajya Sabha.
  • Seventh Schedule:
    • It defines the division of powers between the Union and State governments through three lists:
      • Union List: Subjects under exclusive legislative control of the Parliament (e.g., defense, foreign affairs).
      • State List: Subjects under exclusive legislative control of State Legislatures (e.g., police, public health).
      • Concurrent List: Subjects where both Union and State governments can legislate (e.g., education, marriage).
    • It is crucial for maintaining the federal structure of India.

Important Points

  • Schedules in the Indian Constitution:
    • There are 12 schedules in the Indian Constitution, each dealing with specific aspects of governance and administration.
    • The schedules were originally 8 at the time of adoption of the Constitution in 1950, and additional schedules were added through amendments.
  • Examples of other schedules:

questions.questionHtml:
Read the below statements:
Statement I: The 'Zoji La pass' serves as a very important link between the Kashmir Valley and the Ladakh region, cutting through the Great Himalayan Range.
Statement II: The ‘Shipki La pass’ is located in Arunachal Pradesh and serves as a primary gateway for the river Brahmaputra to enter India from Tibet.

options.html: Neither Statement I nor II is correct

options.text: Both Statement I and II are correct
options.html: Both Statement I and II are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only Statement I is correct.

Key Points

  • Statement I: The Zoji La Pass is a crucial mountain pass located in the Great Himalayan Range. It connects the Kashmir Valley with the Ladakh region. This pass is extremely important for strategic, cultural, and economic links between the two regions. Statement I is correct.
  • Zoji La Pass is located on the Srinagar-Leh highway (NH-1D) and is one of the highest mountain passes in India, with an elevation of approximately 3,528 meters (11,575 feet).
  • It acts as a lifeline for the people of Ladakh, especially during summer months when it remains open for vehicular traffic. However, during winters, heavy snowfall often leads to its closure.
  • Statement II: The Shipki La Pass is not located in Arunachal Pradesh. It is situated in the Himachal Pradesh state, near the Indo-China border. This pass serves as a trade route between India and Tibet, but it is unrelated to the Brahmaputra River. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.
  • The Brahmaputra River enters India from Tibet near the Namcha Barwa mountain range, through a region called Arunachal Pradesh, but this is not connected to Shipki La Pass.

Additional Information

  • Zoji La Pass:
    • Located in the Union Territory of Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir, it is vital for connecting Leh and Srinagar.
    • Historically, this pass has been an essential route for trade and military movements. It is one of the most treacherous roads in the world due to its narrow and steep terrain.
    • The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) maintains the pass, ensuring connectivity during favorable weather conditions.
    • The Zoji La Tunnel is under construction to ensure year-round connectivity, irrespective of snowfall.
  • Shipki La Pass:
    • It is located in the Himachal Pradesh state, near the Indo-China border in the Kinnaur district.
    • This pass facilitates limited trade between India and Tibet, with goods like wool and rock salt historically exchanged.
    • Shipki La is situated at an altitude of approximately 4,720 meters (15,500 feet).
    • The Sutlej River, which originates in Tibet, enters India through Shipki La Pass.
  • Brahmaputra River:
    • The Brahmaputra River originates from the Angsi Glacier in Tibet and flows into India through Arunachal Pradesh.
    • It enters India near the region of Namcha Barwa and is locally known as the Siang River in Arunachal Pradesh.
    • The river is one of the longest in the world, with a total length of approximately 2,900 kilometers.
    • It plays a crucial role in the socio-economic development of northeastern India, particularly in Assam.
  • Important Mountain Passes in India:
    • Rohtang Pass: Located in Himachal Pradesh and connects Kullu Valley with Lahaul and Spiti.
    • Banihal Pass: Connects Jammu with the Kashmir Valley.
    • Nathu La Pass: Located in Sikkim:, it connects India with Tibet and is part of the ancient Silk Route.
    • Lipulekh Pass: Situated in Uttarakhand, it connects India with Tibet and Nepal.

Important Points

  • Strategic Significance of Passes:
    • Mountain passes are crucial for military logistics, trade routes, and cultural exchanges.
    • They often serve as natural borders between nations and regions.
  • Geographical Importance:
    • Passes like Zoji La and Shipki La are vital for connectivity and transportation in mountainous regions.
    • They also play a role in hydrological systems, such as rivers flowing through them.

questions.question: Which indicator is used to measure the 'Knowledge' dimension of the Human Development Index?
questions.questionHtml: Which indicator is used to measure the 'Knowledge' dimension of the Human Development Index?

options.text: Mean years of schooling and Expected years of schooling
options.html: Mean years of schooling and Expected years of schooling

options.text: Adult literacy rate and primary school enrollment
options.html: Adult literacy rate and primary school enrollment

options.text: Number of universities and research publications

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mean years of schooling and Expected years of schooling.

Key Points

  • Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite index published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to measure and rank countries' levels of social and economic development.
  • The HDI comprises three dimensions: Health, Knowledge, and Standard of Living.
  • The Knowledge dimension is assessed using two indicators: Mean years of schooling (average number of years of education received by people aged 25 and older) and Expected years of schooling (the number of years of schooling a child entering school can expect to receive).
  • These indicators reflect both the current educational attainment of adults and the future educational prospects of children, providing a holistic view of a nation's educational development.
  • The use of these two metrics ensures that disparities in education levels across age groups and generations are captured effectively in the HDI calculation.

Additional Information

  • Alternative Indicators:
    • Student-to-teacher ratio in secondary education: While this indicator reflects the quality of education, it does not directly measure the knowledge dimension of HDI.
    • Adult literacy rate and primary school enrollment: These indicators were used in older versions of HDI but were replaced to provide a more comprehensive understanding of educational outcomes.
    • Number of universities and research publications: These are important for assessing higher education and research but are not part of the HDI framework.
  • Calculation of HDI:
    • The three dimensions of HDI are aggregated using a geometric mean to ensure equal importance to all dimensions.
    • Each dimension is expressed as a normalized value between 0 and 1, with higher values indicating better performance.
  • Global Rankings:
    • Countries like Norway, Switzerland, and Ireland consistently rank high in HDI due to strong performance across health, education, and income indicators.
    • Countries with low HDI scores often face challenges such as limited access to education, poor healthcare, and low incomes.
  • Historical Evolution:
    • HDI was introduced in the 1990 Human Development Report by economist Mahbub ul Haq and Nobel laureate Amartya Sen.
    • The inclusion of Mean years of schooling and Expected years of schooling started in 2010 to enhance the accuracy of the index.

Important Points

  • Mean years of schooling:
    • Represents the average number of years of education completed by individuals aged 25 years and older in a country.
    • This indicator provides a snapshot of the educational attainment of adults and reflects the cumulative impact of a nation’s educational policies over time.
  • Expected years of schooling:
    • Estimates the total number of years a child entering school is likely to spend in education, assuming the current enrollment patterns remain unchanged.
    • This metric reflects the potential future educational opportunities for children in a country.
  • HDI in India:
    • India ranked 132 out of 191 countries in the 2021-22 Human Development Report.
    • Challenges include improving access to quality education, reducing dropout rates, and addressing regional disparities in educational outcomes.

questions.question: From a macroeconomic perspective, which indicator best captures the government’s borrowing requirement excluding interest payments on past debt?
questions.questionHtml: From a macroeconomic perspective, which indicator best captures the government’s borrowing requirement excluding interest payments on past debt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Primary Deficit.

Key Points

  • Primary Deficit refers to the fiscal deficit of a government excluding interest payments on past debt. It indicates the borrowing requirement for current expenditures.
  • This metric is important for assessing whether the government's current spending (excluding debt servicing) is sustainable or not.
  • The formula to calculate the primary deficit is: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.
  • It helps in understanding the fiscal stance of the government, i.e., whether the government is borrowing to meet its operational expenses or only to service past debt.
  • In simpler terms, a lower or zero primary deficit means that a government is borrowing mainly for interest payments on its previous debt, rather than for new expenditures.

Additional Information

  • Budget Deficit:
    • The budget deficit is the difference between the total revenue and total expenditure of the government.
    • It includes all revenue and expenditure, irrespective of whether they are capital or revenue-related.
    • It does not specifically exclude interest payments.
    • It is a broader term compared to primary deficit and fiscal deficit.
  • Fiscal Deficit:
    • The fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and total revenue (excluding borrowings).
    • It indicates the total borrowing requirement of the government in a financial year.
    • This metric includes interest payments, which makes it larger than the primary deficit.
    • Example: If a government has high fiscal deficit, it means it is borrowing heavily to finance its expenditure.
  • Revenue Deficit:
    • The revenue deficit refers to the shortfall in revenue receipts compared to revenue expenditures.
    • It highlights the inability of the government to meet its current expenses from its revenue receipts.
    • It does not include capital receipts or expenditures, making it narrower in scope.
  • Importance of Primary Deficit:
    • Primary deficit is a key indicator used to evaluate the financial health of a country.
    • For developing countries, managing primary deficit is crucial to avoid excessive debt accumulation.
    • It also helps policymakers determine whether fiscal policies need adjustments to stabilize the economy.

Important Points

  • Key Terminologies:
    • Interest Payments: The payments made by the government on its accumulated debt over the years.
    • Debt Servicing: The process of repaying the interest and principal amount on borrowed funds.
  • Significance in India:
    • India regularly monitors its fiscal and primary deficits as part of economic planning.
    • The government aims to reduce primary deficit to ensure sustainable fiscal policies.
    • The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act guides India’s fiscal deficit targets and strategies.

Key Points

  • Digitization Process:

  • Global Dissemination:
    • Online platforms are being developed to make manuscripts freely accessible to scholars worldwide.
    • Partnerships with international institutions promote cross-cultural research on India's ancient knowledge systems.
  • Examples of Similar Initiatives:

    • Institutes like Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) are actively involved in manuscript conservation and research.

Important Points

  • Collaborations:

    • To establish centers of excellence for manuscript studies across India.
    • To integrate ancient knowledge with modern educational frameworks.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of enabling encryption for data in transit on a network?
questions.questionHtml: What is the primary benefit of enabling encryption for data in transit on a network?

options.text: It protects against physical theft of devices
options.html: It protects against physical theft of devices

options.text: It ensures that data is unreadable to attackers during transmission
options.html: It ensures that data is unreadable to attackers during transmission

options.text: It improves the overall speed of data transfer
options.html: It improves the overall speed of data transfer

options.text: It prevents unauthorized users from accessing the network
options.html: It prevents unauthorized users from accessing the network

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It ensures that data is unreadable to attackers during transmission.

Key Points

  • Encryption for data in transit involves converting readable data into an unreadable format using encryption algorithms. This ensures that even if the data is intercepted, it cannot be understood without the decryption key.
  • Data in transit refers to data actively moving across networks, such as emails, files, or messages being sent from one device to another.
  • The primary benefit of encryption during transmission is protection against eavesdropping. Attackers who intercept the data cannot read or misuse it without the encryption key.
  • Encryption secures sensitive information such as financial transactions, medical records, and business communications, ensuring privacy and confidentiality.
  • Protocols like HTTPS, SSL/TLS, and VPN use encryption to secure data during transmission. These technologies are widely implemented in web browsing, online banking, and remote work environments.

Additional Information

  • Data Encryption:
    • Encryption is a method of securing data using mathematical algorithms to transform readable text into an unreadable format.
    • Symmetric encryption uses a single key for both encryption and decryption, while asymmetric encryption uses a pair of public and private keys.
    • Examples of encryption algorithms include AES (Advanced Encryption Standard), RSA, and DES.
  • Common Security Protocols:
    • HTTPS: Secures web communications by encrypting data exchanged between browsers and websites using SSL/TLS.
    • SSL/TLS: Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) and Transport Layer Security (TLS) are cryptographic protocols ensuring secure communication over a computer network.
    • VPN: Virtual Private Networks encrypt data transmitted between devices and servers to protect against interception.
  • Importance of Encryption:
    • Encryption helps protect against man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks, where attackers intercept and alter communications.
    • It ensures compliance with data protection laws such as the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) and HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act).
  • Other Security Measures:
    • In addition to encryption, security measures like firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS), and multi-factor authentication (MFA) enhance network security.
    • Regularly updating software and hardware ensures protection against vulnerabilities and exploits.

Important Points

  • Option 1: "It protects against physical theft of devices" is incorrect because encryption of data in transit does not address physical device security.
  • Option 3: "It improves the overall speed of data transfer" is incorrect because encryption can slightly reduce speed due to computational overhead.
  • Option 4: "It prevents unauthorized users from accessing the network" is incorrect because encryption focuses on data protection during transmission, not network access control.
  • Encryption ensures that the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted data remain intact, even if intercepted.

questions.question: In enterprise storage, how does a "Copy-on-Write" (CoW) snapshot differ from a traditional backup?
questions.questionHtml: In enterprise storage, how does a "Copy-on-Write" (CoW) snapshot differ from a traditional backup?

options.text: It is stored on a physically separate secondary device.
options.html: It is stored on a physically separate secondary device.

options.text: It only stores pointers to data blocks until those blocks are modified.
options.html: It only stores pointers to data blocks until those blocks are modified.

options.text: It requires the system to be offline during the process.
options.html: It requires the system to be offline during the process.

options.text: It creates a full bit-by-bit clone of the data immediately.
options.html: It creates a full bit-by-bit clone of the data immediately.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It only stores pointers to data blocks until those blocks are modified..

Key Points

  • Copy-on-Write (CoW) snapshots work by initially storing only pointers to the original data blocks. When a modification is made, the system creates a new block to store the updated data, leaving the original data untouched.
  • This approach is highly efficient in terms of storage space, as no duplicate data blocks are created until changes occur. Only the modified blocks take up additional space.
  • Unlike a traditional backup, which involves creating a full copy of the data, a CoW snapshot is a lightweight process that happens almost instantaneously.
  • CoW snapshots are often used for fast data recovery, as they allow users to access the state of data at a specific point in time without creating an entirely new dataset.
  • They are commonly implemented in modern enterprise storage systems, such as virtualized environments and cloud storage solutions, to ensure data integrity and reduce overhead.

Additional Information

  • Difference Between CoW Snapshots and Traditional Backups:
    • Traditional Backup: Involves creating a full copy of the entire dataset, consuming significant time and storage resources. It is typically stored on separate physical devices to ensure redundancy.
    • Copy-on-Write Snapshot: Only stores pointers to the original data and creates new copies of modified blocks when changes occur. It is faster and more storage-efficient compared to traditional backups.
  • Applications of CoW Snapshots:
    • Used in databases for quick rollback to a consistent state during failures.
    • Widely applied in virtualized environments for creating clones of virtual machines without consuming excessive storage.
    • Enables testing and development environments to work on data copies without affecting the original dataset.
  • Advantages of CoW Snapshots:
    • Efficient storage utilization, as unchanged data blocks are not duplicated.
    • Faster creation and deletion processes compared to traditional backups.
    • Provides point-in-time recovery for data protection and disaster recovery.
  • Limitations of CoW Snapshots:
    • Snapshots are not a substitute for full backups, as they rely on the original dataset. If the original data is lost, the snapshots become unusable.
    • Performance overhead may occur when frequent modifications result in multiple copy-on-write operations.
  • Examples of Systems Using CoW Snapshots:
    • File systems like ZFS and Btrfs implement CoW for efficient snapshots and data integrity.
    • Virtualization platforms such as VMware vSphere and Hyper-V utilize CoW-based snapshots for virtual machine management.

Important Points

  • Option 1: This describes a traditional backup process where data is stored on a separate device. This is not applicable to CoW snapshots.
  • Option 3: CoW snapshots do not require the system to be offline. This statement is incorrect.
  • Option 4: Creating a full bit-by-bit clone of data immediately refers to cloning, not CoW snapshots. This statement is incorrect.

questions.question: In Windows 10/11, which shortcut key combination allows a user to cycle through apps on the Taskbar in the order they are pinned?

  • The Windows Key + T shortcut is used in Windows 10/11 to cycle through applications pinned on the Taskbar sequentially. This functionality enhances productivity by allowing users to easily navigate apps without using a mouse.
  • When you press Windows Key + T, the focus shifts to the first pinned app on the Taskbar. Subsequent presses move the focus to the next app in the sequence.
  • Once the desired app is highlighted, you can press Enter to open it or activate it if it is already running.
  • This shortcut is particularly useful for users who prefer keyboard navigation and want to avoid using a mouse to switch between pinned applications.
  • The functionality is different from Alt + Tab, which cycles through all open windows, not just the pinned Taskbar items.

Additional Information

  • Windows Key + Tab:
    • This shortcut opens the Task View, which displays all open windows and virtual desktops.
    • It allows users to manage virtual desktops or switch between open applications visually.
    • The Task View was introduced in Windows 10 to enhance multitasking capabilities.
  • Alt + Tab:
    • The Alt + Tab shortcut cycles through all open windows, including apps that are not pinned to the Taskbar.
    • It provides a quick way to switch between active tasks without using the mouse.
    • Pressing Alt while tapping Tab displays a visual preview of all open windows.
  • Ctrl + Alt + Tab:
    • This shortcut is similar to Alt + Tab, but the window selection remains active even after releasing the keys, allowing users to use arrow keys or the mouse to choose a window.
    • It is designed for users who prefer a slower-paced method for switching between applications.
  • Taskbar Navigation:
    • Using keyboard shortcuts for Taskbar navigation, such as Windows Key + T, improves efficiency for power users.
    • Other related shortcuts include Windows Key + Number, where the number corresponds to the position of the pinned app on the Taskbar (e.g., Windows Key + 1 opens the first pinned app).

Important Points

  • Windows Key + T is specifically designed for navigating pinned Taskbar items sequentially, making it distinct from other window-switching shortcuts.
  • Shortcuts like Alt + Tab and Ctrl + Alt + Tab are focused on all open windows rather than pinned Taskbar applications.
  • Understanding these keyboard shortcuts can significantly improve multitasking efficiency, especially for users who handle multiple applications simultaneously.
